claim: The drone that hit a car in Lithuania on 18 October entered from Poland
claimed_by: Lithuania (president and prime minister)
evidence: Lithuanian radar track with a minute-by-minute timeline
conflict: Poland says its radars show no crossing. Ukraine says Russian jamming may have diverted it. Russian outlet EADaily spins it as Lithuania letting Ukrainian drones through.
verdict_note: Most likely a stray Ukrainian drone. Two NATO allies disagree on its route.

claim: The Pentagon asked the Baltic states to tone down their rhetoric on Russia
claimed_by: Reuters (four anonymous sources)
conflict: Pentagon declined to comment but did not deny. Baltic ministries silent.
verdict_note: Credible but not confirmed on the record.

claim: Russia could make a limited attack on a NATO country in the coming months
claimed_by: Danish intelligence (25 September); US intelligence via WSJ and CNN (August)
conflict: Estonia's intelligence service: no intention to attack NATO this year. Putin: no plans to attack.
verdict_note: Services disagree on the odds but agree the risk is low and growing. Hybrid escalation is the more likely path.

claim: Russia is adding 16,000–20,000 military hospital beds near the Baltic states
claimed_by: Militarnyi, citing anonymous sources in Russian media; amplified by others
conflict: No official or imagery confirmation. Beds are also planned around Moscow and Smolensk, which fits Ukraine casualties.
verdict_note: Single source; headlines saying beds are moving 'close to the Baltics' overstate it.

claim: Belarus is preparing infrastructure for a Russian push to the Suwałki Gap by spring 2027
claimed_by: BELPOL (exiled Belarusian security officers)
conflict: No official confirmation or denial.
verdict_note: Plausible but partisan. Watch for imagery of rail and communications works.

claim: Ships at Baltiysk signal a Kaliningrad build-up for an attack
claimed_by: YouTube commentary channels
evidence: Imagery shows equipment being loaded out
conflict: OSINT analysts and Militarnyi: destination unknown; the same ships have supplied Africa before.
verdict_note: The imagery is real; the framing is not supported by it.

claim: NATO is preparing an air and naval blockade of Kaliningrad
claimed_by: Russian embassies and a diplomatic note to NATO (late September)
conflict: NATO replied that none of its exercises threaten Russian territory.
verdict_note: No evidence offered. Reads as a pretext narrative backing nuclear warnings.

claim: The Pentagon asked the Baltic states to tone down their rhetoric on Russia
claimed_by: Reuters (four anonymous sources)
conflict: Estonia's foreign minister: no official US proposal. Estonia's PM: allies are asking Estonia to hold back. Peskov: reports should be taken with a grain of salt. Pentagon declines to comment. Lithuania and Latvia silent.
verdict_note: Still unconfirmed on the record, but Estonian reactions suggest informal pressure rather than a formal request.

claim: Russian intelligence was behind the Starlink arson attacks in Poland, Bulgaria and Lithuania
claimed_by: Poland's intelligence minister; Lithuania's prime minister; Der Spiegel
evidence: Official statements; arrests in four countries; press reports on the gang leader's protection in Russia
conflict: Lithuanian police say the ultimate motive has not been established. German broadcaster ARD notes that gang membership is hard to establish. Russia routinely denies such accusations.
verdict_note: The cross-border link is official; the Russian tasking is asserted by officials but not yet shown in court.

claim: Russia will demand a NATO pullback to 1997 lines in peace talks
claimed_by: The Telegraph (unnamed diplomatic sources)
conflict: Not announced by the Kremlin. The Kremlin ruled out European participation in the Abu Dhabi round on 29 October, while the report says Moscow wants Europeans at the table.
verdict_note: Plausible given Russia's 2021 demands, but a single anonymous-source report.

claim: The Kaliningrad blackout was caused by a protection system tripping at the CHP-2 power plant
claimed_by: Kaliningrad regional authorities; grid operator Rosseti
conflict: Ukrainian outlets say the cause could not be verified; social media posts speculated about sabotage without evidence.
verdict_note: The official explanation is plausible and not contradicted by any evidence, but it has not been independently verified.

claim: Russia does not want a war with Europe
claimed_by: Putin (29 October)
conflict: Danish and US intelligence see a low but growing risk of a limited test of NATO; European officials blame Russia for an ongoing sabotage campaign.
verdict_note: Statements of intent cannot be verified; the hybrid record runs against the reassurance.

claim: Belarus is relaying signals for Russian attack drones
claimed_by: Ukraine's border guard spokesperson and military intelligence chief; Ukrainian monitoring project E-radar
conflict: Minsk has not responded. No NATO or Lithuanian technical body has confirmed it. Ukrainian explanations (commercial LTE networks or purpose-built relays) differ.
verdict_note: Relevant to the Baltics because a Russian Gerbera drone was shot down over Lithuania in September; all sources are Ukrainian or Belarusian opposition.

claim: The US is pressing Lithuania to allow Belarusian potash transit despite EU sanctions
claimed_by: Politico (four anonymous European officials)
conflict: Lithuanian PM said in September no US request had been received. The State Department did not respond. Lithuanian officials reject the idea on the record.
verdict_note: Consistent with earlier reporting of US outreach to Minsk; the request itself is not on the record.

claim: The Pentagon asked the Baltic states to tone down their rhetoric on Russia
claimed_by: Reuters (four anonymous sources)
conflict: Lithuania's defence minister says he has no information about such a request. Estonia's PM says no such complaints reached him directly; Estonia's foreign minister and ministry secretary general know of no official request. Pentagon and NATO decline to comment. Latvia silent.
verdict_note: Moved from Likely: two governments now say on the record that no request reached them, though they deny only official or direct requests and Reuters described informal ones.

claim: Russia will demand a NATO pullback to 1997 lines in peace talks
claimed_by: The Telegraph (unnamed diplomatic sources); ISW says the Kremlin has renewed this demand
conflict: ISW's statement cites its own earlier assessments, not a new primary Russian statement. The Kremlin wants Europeans excluded from the talks, while the Telegraph says Moscow wants them at the table.
verdict_note: Consistent with Russia's long-standing 2021 position, but no Russian official has been shown making it as a formal demand in the current talks.

claim: The Belarusian government organises illegal migration into the Baltic states
claimed_by: Estonian and Latvian interior ministers (30 October)
conflict: Minsk has not responded in the available reporting; it has denied such accusations in the past. Armed, masked escorts at Latvia's border in early October support the claim.
verdict_note: Consistent with years of official findings in Poland, Lithuania and Latvia, though direct proof of state direction is rarely published.

claim: A Russian national arrested in Świdnica was gathering rail intelligence for a foreign service
claimed_by: Polish police and prosecutors
conflict: The intelligence service has not been named and the charge has not been tested in court. No Russian response reported.
verdict_note: A formal charge backed by seized material, but still an accusation; the suspect is presumed innocent.

claim: Men are being seized off the streets in Russian cities and pressed to sign army contracts
claimed_by: Meduza, iStories, Verstka; relatives and rights groups
conflict: No official confirmation or response from Russian authorities in the reporting. Most accounts are second-hand.
verdict_note: Several independent outlets and complaints from many regions point the same way.

claim: Russia wants fully-fledged relations with European countries
claimed_by: Putin (29 October)
conflict: Moscow simultaneously demands that European leaders stay out of peace talks, and European governments blame Russia for an ongoing sabotage campaign.
verdict_note: A statement of intent that cannot be verified and that Russia's hybrid record contradicts.

claim: Belarusian state structures may be coordinating sabotage in Europe alongside Russian intelligence
claimed_by: Robert Lansing Institute (commentary)
conflict: The piece itself says state complicity is not established; the only fact behind it is that two suspects detained in Germany are Belarusian citizens. German prosecutors have not named a client.
verdict_note: A hypothesis from an outlet that does not disclose its funding; no official or evidence-based source supports Belarusian state involvement.

claim: The object that entered eastern Latvia on 1 November was a stray Ukrainian drone
claimed_by: Implied by Izvestia's headline and related links; Latvian armed forces call it only an unidentified object
conflict: Latvia has named neither the type nor the origin. The Kyiv Independent says it was likely a drone of unclear origin. Earlier stray drones over Latvia were both Ukrainian and Russian.
verdict_note: No official identification yet; the object left toward Russia, which by itself proves nothing about where it came from.

claim: The Pentagon asked the Baltic states to tone down their rhetoric on Russia
claimed_by: Reuters (four anonymous sources)
conflict: Lithuania's defence minister and Estonia's PM say no such request reached them; Estonia's foreign ministry knows of no official request. A former Estonian diplomat now argues the message should be more measured anyway. Pentagon silent.
verdict_note: No new evidence either way; the Estonian debate is about style, not about whether a request was made.

claim: Russia is building an over-the-horizon radar near Gvardeysk that could watch NATO aircraft across much of Europe
claimed_by: ICEYE imagery via FAZ and Stars and Stripes; amplified by the Robert Lansing Institute
conflict: The construction is visible on imagery, but the range and purpose are projections, and whether it is operational is unknown. No Russian or NATO comment.
verdict_note: Construction is well supported by imagery; the capability claims are not yet confirmed.

claim: Russia is plotting to kill European defence-industry executives
claimed_by: Representatives of five EU intelligence agencies (to the Financial Times), summarised by Al Jazeera
conflict: No named official or court case in the reporting describes a specific plot. Moscow denies running sabotage in Europe.
verdict_note: Consistent with earlier reported plots and with incendiary devices found at Munich offices, but the central claim rests on unnamed officials.

claim: Russia will demand a NATO pullback to 1997 lines in peace talks
claimed_by: The Telegraph (unnamed diplomatic sources); ISW says the Kremlin has renewed this demand
conflict: ISW's 31 October assessment again cites the demand without a fresh primary Russian statement. No Russian official has been shown making it as a formal demand in the current talks.
verdict_note: No new evidence since yesterday; consistent with Russia's 2021 position but still unconfirmed as a demand in talks.

claim: Armed groups could try to cross from Kaliningrad into Poland in the coming days
claimed_by: RMF, citing unnamed sources on warnings from Poland's Military Intelligence Service and allied agencies
conflict: The police chief confirmed on the record only a general sabotage threat and did not mention armed groups. Authorities call the operation preventive; no incident has been reported. No Russian response found.
verdict_note: The operation is real; the specific armed-incursion scenario rests on anonymous sources.

claim: A Russian citizen deported from Estonia kept contacts with Russian intelligence officers
claimed_by: Estonia's Internal Security Service (KAPO)
conflict: KAPO has not published its evidence and the case has not been tested in court. No public response from the man or from Moscow found.
verdict_note: An on-the-record claim by a security service with a strong track record, but the evidence is not public.

claim: The object that entered eastern Latvia on 1 November was a stray Ukrainian drone
claimed_by: Implied by Izvestia's headline and related links; Latvian armed forces call it only an unidentified object
conflict: Latvia still names neither type nor origin. Its interceptor self-destructed without reaching the object, so there is no wreckage to examine. Earlier stray drones over Latvia were both Ukrainian and Russian.
verdict_note: No new evidence on origin; the exit toward Russia by itself proves nothing.

claim: Russian electronic warfare pushed the drone that fell in Lithuania on 18 October off course
claimed_by: Ukraine's foreign ministry spokesperson, as reported by European Pravda
conflict: Lithuania says the drone came in from Poland and carried explosives; Ukraine expressed regret, implying it was Ukrainian, and blamed Russian jamming. No independent technical finding on the cause has been published.
verdict_note: Plausible given persistent Russian jamming in the region, but it is the explanation of the drone's operator, not an independent finding.

claim: The people seen with flashlights near Sępopol were attempting a Russian provocation
claimed_by: Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk, hedged: he said this was so 'if that was the intention'
conflict: Nobody crossed the border and no one has been identified. Tusk himself said he could not be fully certain. Russia's embassy calls the sabotage warnings fake; no Russian comment on the incident itself.
verdict_note: The sighting is confirmed; its purpose is not.

claim: Polish and allied intelligence warned of possible incursions by armed people from Kaliningrad in the first half of November
claimed_by: Donald Tusk on the record; earlier RMF citing unnamed sources; AP says warnings came from Polish, NATO, Ukrainian and US services
conflict: Yesterday this rested on anonymous sources; the prime minister has now confirmed the content of the warnings on the record. The underlying intelligence is not public, and Russia dismisses it as fake.
verdict_note: That the warnings were given is now well established; whether such an incursion was really planned cannot be judged from public evidence.

claim: The drone that entered eastern Latvia on 1 November was a Russian Geran
claimed_by: Latvia's armed forces (most likely assessment); earlier, Izvestia's framing implied a stray Ukrainian drone
conflict: The drone flew back into Russia and no wreckage exists, so the assessment rests on tracking data. Russian state media had linked the alert to Ukrainian drones; no Russian official has commented on Latvia's new assessment.
verdict_note: An on-the-record military assessment; it outweighs the earlier implication of a Ukrainian origin, which had no evidence behind it.

claim: The drone over Balvi on 3 November was Ukrainian
claimed_by: Latvia's armed forces, on initial visual identification
conflict: Latvia says the exact type and origin are not established, and the wreckage has not been found. Ukraine has not commented.
verdict_note: Plausible, given Ukraine's attacks on Russian Baltic ports, but provisional until wreckage is found.

claim: Polish warnings about possible sabotage are fake news driven by militarist rhetoric
claimed_by: Russia's embassy in Warsaw, via TASS
conflict: Several services, according to Tusk and AP, issued the warnings independently. Poland has not published the evidence, but Russia offers none for its denial either.
verdict_note: A blanket denial with no evidence, from a government whose earlier denials of sabotage in Poland were contradicted by Polish investigations.

claim: The people seen with flashlights near Sępopol were attempting a Russian provocation
claimed_by: Implied by Donald Tusk; Polish and Ukrainian media headlines
conflict: Tusk said he could not be certain; Siemoniak said he could not confirm the warned plan involved crossing from Kaliningrad. Russia calls the warnings fake. No further details have been released.
verdict_note: The sighting is real; its purpose remains unknown, and no new evidence has emerged.

claim: Polish and allied intelligence warned of possible incursions by armed people from Kaliningrad in the first half of November
claimed_by: Donald Tusk on the record; Stars and Stripes names NATO commander Alexus Grynkewich among those who warned; Tomasz Siemoniak
conflict: Several officials confirm the warnings were given, but Siemoniak calls them imprecise. The underlying intelligence is not public, and Russia dismisses it as fake.
verdict_note: That the warnings were given is well established; whether an incursion was really planned cannot be judged from public evidence.

claim: A planned provocation on the Kaliningrad border would be staged so that Ukrainians are blamed
claimed_by: Tomasz Siemoniak, Polish minister coordinating special services (TVN24)
conflict: No evidence has been published, and the minister himself called the information imprecise. Russian outlets have long pushed narratives that blame Ukraine for incidents in Poland and the Baltics, which makes the scenario plausible but not proven.
verdict_note: A serious official warning about possible intent, not evidence of an operation.

claim: Russian intelligence was behind the 23 September arson at a Starlink ground station near Warsaw
claimed_by: Polish government; Der Spiegel reporting on the investigation
conflict: Arrests in Germany and charges in several countries back the criminal case, but the Russian link rests on Polish attribution and press reports of a Turkish crime group that may have worked for Russian services. Russia has not commented on this case.
verdict_note: Consistent with a well-documented pattern of Russian proxy sabotage, but not yet proven in court.

claim: Poland's Kaliningrad border operation is a political distraction from Tusk's domestic troubles
claimed_by: RT (Russian state media); earlier the Russian embassy in Warsaw
conflict: The warnings came from several allied services, including NATO's commander, and US and German forces have separately tightened their own security. RT offers no evidence for its motive claim.
verdict_note: A motive claim with no supporting evidence that ignores the allied sources of the warnings.

claim: NATO is an aggressive bloc preparing for war with Russia, while Russia and Belarus intend to attack no one
claimed_by: Alexander Lukashenko at the Minsk security conference (Izvestia)
conflict: NATO's public plans are built around deterring and repelling an attack. Lithuania's threat assessment judges that Russia could in the longer term carry out limited operations against NATO states, and Russia gave similar assurances before invading Ukraine in 2022.
verdict_note: Turns allied defensive preparations into proof of aggression and offers assurances contradicted by recent history.

claim: Poland and the Baltic states are training people to work for Russia's collapse from within
claimed_by: Sergei Shoigu, Secretary of Russia's Security Council; echoed by Maria Zakharova
conflict: No evidence offered. Poland, Lithuania, Germany and Romania have published arrests and court cases showing the reverse flow: people recruited by Russian services for spying and sabotage in Europe.
verdict_note: A mirror-image accusation with no evidence, timed after Polish and Lithuanian disclosures.

claim: Three Ukrainians in Lithuania carried out paid tasks for hostile foreign intelligence services
claimed_by: Lithuania's State Security Department (VSD)
conflict: The VSD did not name the services, open a criminal case or publish evidence; the three cannot contest it in Lithuania now that they have left. The method described matches earlier proven cases.
verdict_note: A credible official finding matching a known pattern, but untested in court and with the sponsor unnamed.

claim: Six people detained in Poland supplied Russia with military components, and four spied for Russia
claimed_by: Polish Internal Security Agency (ABW); minister Tomasz Siemoniak
conflict: Backed by searches and a court custody order; details of the evidence are not public. No Russian response.
verdict_note: An active criminal case with judicial oversight; guilt not yet established.

claim: A man living in Russia coordinated a 2024 plot to attack Romanian oil and gas sites
claimed_by: Romanian anti-terrorism prosecutors (DIICOT); Bucharest Court of Appeals
conflict: The hired accomplice was convicted in 2025, which supports the plot itself; the coordinator's role and the Russian connection rest on the prosecution's case, as he is beyond Romania's reach.
verdict_note: The plot is established in court; the coordinator's guilt and the sponsorship are not yet tested.

claim: Polish and allied intelligence warned of possible incursions by armed people from Kaliningrad in the first half of November
claimed_by: Donald Tusk; Tomasz Siemoniak; NATO commander Alexus Grynkewich (per Stars and Stripes)
conflict: No confirmed crossing attempt since the warnings; Poland's operation continues until at least 8 November. Russia calls the warnings fake and Shoigu now accuses Poland itself of training saboteurs.
verdict_note: That the warnings were given is well established; whether an incursion was planned cannot be judged from public evidence.

claim: GPS interference affected almost all of NATO's eastern flank on 3 November
claimed_by: ItaMilRadar (OSINT), reported by Militarnyi
conflict: Flight-data maps show where aircraft lose accuracy, not who is jamming; part of the interference stems from the war in Ukraine. Baltic governments have long attributed the Kaliningrad-area interference to Russia.
verdict_note: The pattern is well documented; this single map adds a snapshot, not new attribution.

claim: A Russian satellite rehearsed an attack on a Finnish ICEYE radar satellite
claimed_by: Greg Gillinger (Integrity ISR) via Reuters; supported in tone by US Under Secretary Thomas DiNanno; repeated by the Robert Lansing Institute
conflict: Orbital data confirm unusual close approaches, but Germany's space commander says they could be inspection or interference and do not prove an attack plan; the Lansing piece itself says the data do not show preparations for a strike. Reported distances range from 26 metres to about a kilometre. Russia has not commented.
verdict_note: The manoeuvres are documented; the 'rehearsal' reading is plausible but not established.

claim: The Fitburg's officers damaged Finland–Estonia undersea cables with the ship's anchor
claimed_by: Helsinki District Court; Finnish prosecutors
conflict: A first-instance conviction for aggravated criminal damage; an appeal is possible. The court did not find that the Russian state ordered it, and a separate court dismissed charges in the Eagle S case in October.
verdict_note: Tested in court, but not final, and state direction is not established.

claim: US officials pressed Lithuania to allow Belarusian fertiliser transit through Klaipėda
claimed_by: Politico (relayed by LRT)
conflict: A presidential adviser did not deny an approach but called the report outdated; Foreign Minister Kęstutis Budrys denied that any such discussion is taking place. No US comment reported.
verdict_note: An approach may have happened, but the Lithuanian accounts differ and current talks are denied.

claim: Satellite data show Russia partly replenishing self-propelled artillery near Petrozavodsk, about 185 km from Finland
claimed_by: Robert Lansing Institute (citing an 'OCP monitoring system')
conflict: No official, imagery publisher or quality outlet has confirmed it; the source of the data is not identified. The same piece says no strike group was assembled.
verdict_note: Commentary-tier claim with an unclear source; not used for any rating.

claim: Lithuania's border with Kaliningrad is calmer than Poland's
claimed_by: Lithuanian Defence Minister Robertas Kaunas (via LRT)
conflict: Consistent with Lithuania's interior minister saying earlier this week that the threat level had not changed, and with no reported incidents on the Lithuanian side; Poland remains on alert after the 3 November sighting.
verdict_note: Fits all public reporting; based on a short LRT item.

claim: Polish and allied intelligence warned of possible incursions by armed people from Kaliningrad in the first half of November
claimed_by: Donald Tusk; Tomasz Siemoniak; NATO commander Alexus Grynkewich (per Stars and Stripes)
conflict: Still no confirmed crossing attempt; Poland's operation continues until at least 8 November. Russia calls the warnings fake.
verdict_note: That the warnings were given is well established; whether an incursion was planned cannot be judged from public evidence.

claim: The Kraków shooting was a Russian-directed operation
claimed_by: Online speculation, and headlines framing the attack around Russian sabotage fears (e.g. FinChannel); no official
conflict: Polish officials say the suspect acted alone and point to radical, possibly far-right views; no foreign link, financing or network has been announced. The Russian embassy only reported that a Russian citizen was injured.
verdict_note: Nothing in the public evidence supports a Russian link; the investigation is still open.

claim: The Kraków gunman was driven by far-right extremist views
claimed_by: Interior Minister Marcin Kierwiński
conflict: Early findings only; the minister said this still needs investigation. Police dismissed reports of an accomplice and the defence ministry denied he was a soldier.
verdict_note: A preliminary official indication, not yet an established motive.

claim: The Coalition of the Willing drills show London and Paris seek Russia's military defeat
claimed_by: Maria Zakharova, Russian Foreign Ministry (via TASS)
conflict: Polish defence ministry details describe a post-hostilities deployment exercise, outside NATO and without combat or peacekeeping tasks.
verdict_note: The drills are real; the stated purpose contradicts Zakharova's description.

claim: Russia is not seeking good-faith talks in Abu Dhabi
claimed_by: ISW
conflict: Based on the make-up of Russia's delegation and its public rejection of security guarantees and a European role.
verdict_note: Consistent with Russia's on-the-record positions, but intent can only be judged after the talks.

claim: Polish and allied intelligence warned of possible incursions by armed people from Kaliningrad in the first half of November
claimed_by: Donald Tusk; Tomasz Siemoniak; NATO commander Alexus Grynkewich (per Stars and Stripes)
conflict: The operation reached its scheduled end date of 8 November with no confirmed crossing attempt; Russia calls the warnings fake.
verdict_note: That the warnings were given is well established; whether an incursion was planned cannot be judged from public evidence.

claim: The Kraków gunman was linked to Ukraine's International Legion or pro-Azov fighters
claimed_by: Russian Telegram channel Shot and pro-Kremlin accounts on X
conflict: Polish prosecutors identify a Polish citizen acting alone with far-right views; the patch cited is a generic design sold online, not a Ukrainian unit emblem.
verdict_note: Contradicted by official findings and by visual checks of the patch.

claim: The Kraków shooting was a Russian-directed operation
claimed_by: Online speculation and some headlines; no official
conflict: Prosecutors say evidence so far shows no one else was involved; officials name a far-right motive and no foreign link.
verdict_note: Still no public evidence of a Russian role; the investigation continues.

claim: The Kraków gunman acted from far-right extremist motives
claimed_by: Interior Minister Marcin Kierwiński; prosecutors
conflict: Some far-right politicians online dispute the label or claim left-wing or other motives, without evidence.
verdict_note: Now backed by prosecutors, who are treating the attack as terrorism; a final motive awaits the investigation.

claim: The disinformation surge after Kraków was coordinated, with Russian involvement
claimed_by: Deputy PM Krzysztof Gawkowski; NASK data (as reported by European Interest)
conflict: NASK found over 2,000 accounts, many automated, some with Russian markers; but domestic far-right figures pushed some of the same narratives, and no state actor has been formally named.
verdict_note: Coordinated amplification is well supported; Russian state direction is plausible but not proven publicly.

claim: Russia recruits Ukrainian refugees for sabotage in Europe; about 200 Russia-linked sabotage acts since 2022
claimed_by: Ukraine's Foreign Intelligence Service (via Ukrinform)
conflict: Fits European court cases and Lithuania's expulsion of three Ukrainians; the figures are given without a breakdown and come from a party to the war.
verdict_note: The pattern is well documented; the exact numbers are unconfirmed.

claim: Russia used the Oleshky truce to move over 1,000 troops and equipment to the Kherson left bank
claimed_by: Ukrainian military sources (via Militarnyi, Kyiv Post); noted by ISW
conflict: Not confirmed by Russia or independent imagery; ISW reports no major Russian assaults there yet.
verdict_note: A single-side claim; worth watching as a test of how Russia uses truces.

claim: Leaked Rosstat data show 390,000–450,000 Russians killed in the war
claimed_by: Hacker groups Belarus Cyber Partisans and Silent Crow; analysed by The Moscow Times
conflict: The two groups' totals differ by method; The Moscow Times verified a sample of names but not the full dataset; roughly in line with an earlier British estimate.
verdict_note: Plausible and partly checked, but the dataset's integrity cannot yet be confirmed.

claim: Foreign contingents in Ukraine would be military intervention and a foothold against Russia
claimed_by: Maria Zakharova, Russian Foreign Ministry
conflict: UK and French officials say the force would deploy only after a ceasefire, at Kyiv's request, with no combat or peacekeeping mandate and outside NATO.
verdict_note: Repeats earlier framing; the stated purpose of the force contradicts it.

claim: The Kraków gunman acted from far-right extremist motives
claimed_by: Interior Minister Marcin Kierwiński (7–8 November)
conflict: Prosecutors now say the motive is not established and found no symbols of political extremism; the opposition calls the far-right label a lie; unverified online claims of far-left views also circulate (Defence24).
verdict_note: Downgraded from Likely: the government's own prosecutors no longer support the label, and the gunman's death means no trial will test it.

claim: The Kraków shooting was a Russian-directed operation
claimed_by: Online speculation and some headlines; no official
conflict: The justice minister says investigators will check whether anyone helped or inspired the gunman, and a Russian link has reportedly not been excluded, but no evidence has been released.
verdict_note: Still no public evidence of a Russian role.

claim: The Polish government staged the Kraków attack, with EU help, to ban the Independence March
claimed_by: Anonymous accounts and bot networks, including some Russian-language ones
conflict: The prime minister and interior minister deny any plan to ban the march; the attack's victims, the gunman's death and the police response are documented.
verdict_note: No basis; rated false by the Global Security Centre and contradicted by the facts of the case.

claim: Russia-linked hackers were behind the supermarket freezer cyberattacks
claimed_by: Pro-Russian hacker groups NoName057(16) and Z-Pentest Alliance (posts later deleted); researchers quoted by the FT
conflict: The Kremlin calls the idea absurd; the EU calls the attacks deliberate but names no culprit; some analysts doubt the groups' claims.
verdict_note: Plausible given earlier US cases, but no official attribution yet.

claim: Russia is behind about 90% of Estonia's internal security problems
claimed_by: Estonian Interior Minister Igor Taro (to the FT)
conflict: No breakdown given; consistent in direction with Estonian and Lithuanian intelligence reports, but the figure cannot be checked.
verdict_note: A senior official's estimate, not a published finding.

claim: Russia's military presence in the Baltic Sea has probably peaked for now
claimed_by: Finnish Navy commander Rear Admiral Tuomas Tiilikainen (to Sky News)
conflict: Sits alongside Polish warnings that Russian threats will grow; the two are compatible, since one concerns naval presence and the other hybrid pressure.
verdict_note: A credible frontline judgement, matched by the absence of new naval incidents.

claim: Ukraine and Europe want to prolong the war, and Poland and the Baltic states are provocatively expanding NATO infrastructure
claimed_by: Sergei Shoigu, Russian Security Council
conflict: Ukraine calls for an immediate ceasefire, which Russia rejects; NATO's eastern-flank build-up is defensive and followed Russia's 2022 invasion.
verdict_note: Reverses cause and effect; Russia itself rejects a general ceasefire.

claim: The drones that entered Lithuanian and Latvian airspace on 10–11 November were Russian
claimed_by: Implied by Baltic and NATO officials who blame Russia for the incidents; disputed by Kyiv's and Moscow's competing accounts
evidence: Official statements (alerts only); no published identification
conflict: Kyiv says Russian jamming pushes its drones off course; Moscow says Kyiv uses NATO airspace as cover; Baltic authorities have not yet said whose drones these were.
verdict_note: The timing matches Ukraine's strike on the Leningrad region, and earlier strays this year were mostly Ukrainian. No wreckage or official identification has been published.

claim: Kyiv uses Baltic and NATO airspace as cover for its drone attacks on Russia
claimed_by: Russian officials (repeated after the 10–11 November alerts)
conflict: Baltic governments deny allowing their airspace to be used; the EU's foreign policy chief earlier called the claim nonsense. Kyiv blames Russian jamming for strays.
verdict_note: No evidence has been offered that the Baltic states allow or that Ukraine plans routes through NATO airspace; the strays are consistent with jamming and navigation errors.

claim: The balloon-type object from Belarus that closed Vilnius and Kaunas airports is part of a Belarusian hybrid attack
claimed_by: Lithuanian authorities
conflict: Minsk has denied earlier accusations and frames the balloons as smuggling by criminals.
verdict_note: The flights have repeated for over a year with the same effect on airports, and Belarus has not acted against them; whether each launch is state-directed is not proven.

claim: The Kraków gunman acted from far-right extremist motives
claimed_by: Interior Minister Marcin Kierwiński (7–8 November); Justice Minister Waldemar Żurek (10 November)
evidence: Official statements; circumstantial evidence (browsing history, a flag)
conflict: The National Prosecutor's Office says the flag is not tied to any one ideology and the motive is still under investigation, including possible mental illness.
verdict_note: New circumstantial evidence supports the hypothesis, but prosecutors have not confirmed a motive.

claim: NATO keeps up to 30,000 troops in the Baltic region, and new territorial defence units there are revanchist and would move east
claimed_by: Belarusian Foreign Minister Maxim Ryzhenkov (via TASS)
conflict: Allied deployments in the region are defensive and public; the Baltic and Polish territorial defence forces are home-defence units.
verdict_note: The troop figure is plausible in scale, but the framing of defensive units as revanchist has no supporting evidence.

claim: Russian air defences downed 146 drones over the Leningrad region
claimed_by: Leningrad region governor Aleksandr Drozdenko
conflict: Outlets quoting the same official report different totals (81, 92, 141, 146), and fires at Ust-Luga and Kirishi show some drones got through.
verdict_note: Russian intercept tallies are not independently verifiable and changed through the night.

claim: Russia and Ukraine have privately shown some flexibility on territory
claimed_by: A senior US official, via US media
conflict: Publicly, Moscow still demands Ukraine leave all of Donetsk and Kyiv rejects ceding territory it holds.
verdict_note: Single anonymous source repeated widely; no details given.

claim: Two Ukrainian citizens detained in Poland carried out arson and spying for Russian intelligence
claimed_by: Poland's intelligence coordinator and the ABW
conflict: No public response from the suspects; charges not yet tested in court.
verdict_note: Official charges are serious and fit a known pattern, but remain allegations.

claim: The drone that crossed Lithuania on 10–11 November was a stray Ukrainian drone
claimed_by: Lithuanian Defence Staff (as a possibility); Russian state-aligned media (as fact)
evidence: Official assessment; no published identification or wreckage
conflict: Lithuania's defence chief told Reuters it is unconfirmed whether the drone was Ukrainian or Russian; Lenta.ru's headline calls it a Ukrainian army drone; Kyiv blames Russian jamming for strays.
verdict_note: The timing and route fit Ukraine's strike on the Leningrad region and earlier strays were mostly Ukrainian, but the drone was not recovered and no identification has been published.

claim: The drone briefly entered Polish airspace
claimed_by: Head of Lithuania's National Crisis Management Centre
conflict: Poland's Operational Command does not confirm any violation and suggests a weather effect on radar; it is still analysing data.
verdict_note: Two allied official accounts disagree; until Poland finishes its radar review, the Polish leg should not be treated as established.

claim: Lithuania and its neighbours let Ukrainian drones fly through their airspace to attack Russia
claimed_by: Russian officials (repeatedly); social-media posts after the 10–11 November alerts
conflict: Lithuania's crisis-management chief calls it completely false; NATO jets tried twice to shoot this drone down, and Latvia says firing was unsafe, not unwanted.
verdict_note: The attempts to destroy the drone directly contradict the claim that it was allowed through; no evidence of any arrangement has been offered.

claim: The NATO interception failed because of poor weather and the risk to civilians
claimed_by: Lithuanian Defence Staff and crisis centre
conflict: Lithuania's army commander says the country whose jet fired must establish what went wrong with its missile; LRT reports the second attempt had additional problems; a Russian military commentator mocks the pilots.
verdict_note: Plausible and consistent with the conditions reported, but the investigation is open and the defence minister says not all findings will be published.

claim: A drone violated Finnish airspace over the eastern Gulf of Finland on 11 November
claimed_by: Finnish defence ministry
conflict: No contradiction; origin not stated, and the border guard is investigating.
verdict_note: An official finding of a suspected violation lasting about five minutes, on the same night as confirmed incursions in Latvia and Lithuania.

claim: Balloon flights from Belarus are part of a Belarusian hybrid attack
claimed_by: Lithuanian authorities
conflict: Minsk frames the balloons as criminal smuggling; Lithuanian border guards again intercepted three cigarette loads and detained a suspect, showing smuggling is a real motive.
verdict_note: The flights are both smuggling and a pressure tool: Belarus has not stopped them despite repeated airport closures; whether each launch is state-directed is not proven.

claim: The Abu Dhabi talks moved the sides closer to peace
claimed_by: Russian negotiator Vladimir Medinsky; a Ukrainian delegate spoke of good momentum
conflict: The US side cited a lack of trust; Medinsky also says Russia will take 'every inch' it claims and Lavrov restates the 2024 demands; no agreement was announced.
verdict_note: Progress on prisoner exchanges is plausible, but the core territorial and security disputes remain open.

claim: European representatives will take part in the next round of peace talks
claimed_by: US envoy Steve Witkoff
conflict: Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov did not confirm it and called Europe's stance a recipe for endless war; Russia's negotiator has refused to deal with Europeans.
verdict_note: The US says it is agreed, Moscow has not said so, and no date or format has been published.

claim: Bilateral non-aggression pacts would give NATO members extra security guarantees from Russia
claimed_by: Alexei Drobinin, Russian foreign ministry
conflict: Estonia's prime minister calls Moscow's security agenda a trap; Kaja Kallas says the problem is that Russia does not keep the agreements that already exist.
verdict_note: Russia broke earlier commitments to respect its neighbours' borders, including toward Ukraine, so a new pledge offers little verifiable security; the offer to individual states also cuts across NATO's collective defence.

claim: Russia is seeking a pull-back of NATO forces from the eastern flank as part of a settlement
claimed_by: European officials (via the FT); Lithuanian and Estonian leaders
conflict: Moscow frames it as a new European 'security architecture' rather than a withdrawal demand, and has not published its paper.
verdict_note: Russia's own negotiator says the security system was the central topic, and the demand matches Moscow's 2021 proposals restated by Lavrov this week.

claim: The FSB broke up a Polish intelligence network in Kaliningrad
claimed_by: Russia's FSB
evidence: Official statement; video released by the FSB
conflict: Poland's security services call it a provocation and disinformation; Polish fact-checkers point to signs the material was staged or filmed earlier.
verdict_note: The only evidence is material released by the FSB; Poland is still checking it and has not confirmed any arrests.

claim: Ukraine hit a Russian Buyan-M missile ship in the Gulf of Finland
claimed_by: Ukraine's SBU
evidence: Official statement; independent official confirmation of a strike
conflict: Russia has not commented; Finland confirms a strike on a Russian warship but not its type or damage.
verdict_note: Finland's independent detection of a strike makes the claim credible; the identity of the ship and the extent of damage remain unconfirmed.

claim: NATO and Poland are preparing to isolate or seize Kaliningrad
claimed_by: Russian diplomats and officials (since September); framing around the FSB claim
conflict: NATO's secretary general says no alliance activity threatens Russian territory; Poland's border operation is described as defensive, against sabotage.
verdict_note: No evidence has been offered beyond NATO exercises that are announced in advance; the claim serves to justify Russian nuclear warnings.

claim: Russia proposed in Abu Dhabi that Finland leave NATO and that no NATO bases be allowed in Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania
claimed_by: Bild (anonymous sources), repeated by many outlets
conflict: The Kremlin denies the Finland part; Bild itself calls it one of several informal proposals and is unsure Putin backs it; no official on either side has confirmed the Baltic part.
verdict_note: Plausible given Russia's on-record aims, but the specific demands rest on one anonymous-source report and an official denial.

claim: Russia is seeking a pull-back of NATO forces from the eastern flank as part of a settlement
claimed_by: European officials (via the FT and NYT); Lithuanian, Estonian and Finnish leaders
conflict: Russia frames it as a new 'European security architecture'; Peskov denies only the Finland element.
verdict_note: Russia's own negotiator calls the security system the central topic, and Finland's defence minister now describes the demand on the record.

claim: European representatives will take part in the next round of peace talks
claimed_by: US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner; Ukraine's president
conflict: Peskov says Europe must first show readiness to contribute and no decision has been made.
verdict_note: The US and Ukraine say it is agreed; Russia says it is not decided. No date or format has been published.

claim: Russia would withdraw nuclear weapons from Belarus in exchange for NATO concessions
claimed_by: Bild; El País (anonymous sources)
conflict: No Russian or Belarusian official has confirmed it; Russia has not said publicly that its weapons in Belarus are on the table.
verdict_note: Reported only by anonymous sources; if real, it shows the Belarus deployments are being used as bargaining chips, as the baseline suggests.

claim: Ukraine hit a Russian Buyan-M missile ship in the Gulf of Finland
claimed_by: Ukraine's SBU
conflict: Russia has not commented; Finland detected a strike but has not identified the ship.
verdict_note: Finland's independent detection and Estonian reports of a damaged ship returning to St Petersburg make the claim credible; the extent of damage is unknown.

claim: The FSB broke up a Polish intelligence network in Kaliningrad
claimed_by: Russia's FSB
conflict: Polish officials call it a provocation; no new details have been released since 11 November.
verdict_note: The only evidence is material released by the FSB; Poland has not confirmed any arrests.

claim: Lithuania and its neighbours let Ukrainian drones fly through their airspace to attack Russia
claimed_by: Pro-Kremlin social media and commentators
conflict: Lithuania's National Crisis Management Centre calls it completely false; NATO jets tried to shoot down the drone that crossed Lithuania.
verdict_note: The facts point the other way: Lithuania sounded air alerts and NATO tried to destroy the drone.

claim: Russia has put in writing a demand that NATO pull forces and bases back to 1997 positions, which would remove them from Poland, the Baltic states and Finland
claimed_by: The New York Times and The Telegraph (leaked 10 November paper)
conflict: The paper is unsigned and unpublished; the Kremlin has not commented; earlier reports of this demand rested only on anonymous expectations.
verdict_note: Two major outlets describe the same dated paper, one with a copy confirmed by a second source; it matches Russia's 2021 demands.

claim: Russia wants Britain and France not to use their nuclear weapons to protect other European states
claimed_by: The Telegraph; The New York Times
conflict: No Russian official has said this on the record; the UK government has not addressed the point directly.
verdict_note: Both outlets cite the same paper; it is a negotiating demand, not a threat.

claim: Russia asked that Finland leave NATO and that no NATO bases be allowed in Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania
claimed_by: Bild (anonymous sources), repeated by many outlets
conflict: The Kremlin denies the Finland part; accounts of the 10 November paper by the NYT and The Telegraph mention the 1997 pull-back, which covers the Baltic states, but not Finland leaving NATO.
verdict_note: The Baltic part is consistent with the leaked paper; the Finland exit rests on one report and an official denial.

claim: European representatives will take part in the next round of peace talks
claimed_by: US envoys; Ukraine's president; EU leaders
conflict: Bloomberg (via ISW) says five countries and an EU representative were named for technical talks; Euronews reports no agreed EU envoy; the Kremlin says Europe must first show readiness to contribute.
verdict_note: Europe has organised its team, but Russia has not accepted it publicly and no date has been set.

claim: Ukraine hit a Russian Buyan-M missile ship in the Gulf of Finland
claimed_by: Ukraine's SBU; Estonian Defence Forces
conflict: Russia has not commented.
verdict_note: Estonia's military independently says the Naro-Fominsk was hit by several drones, with casualties, and had to be escorted to port.

claim: Ukraine is deliberately routing attack drones through Polish and Baltic airspace
claimed_by: Pro-Kremlin social media and commentators
conflict: Estonia says it never authorised such flights; Lithuania says Russian electronic warfare may have pushed a drone off course; NATO jets tried to shoot one down.
verdict_note: Drones have strayed into Baltic airspace, but no evidence shows deliberate routing or any Baltic consent.

claim: Russia's GRU ordered the attempted arson at Threod Systems in Estonia
claimed_by: Estonia's KAPO and prime minister; supported by Latvia's VDD
conflict: The intelligence behind the attribution has not been published; Russia has not commented on this case and called a similar accusation over the August Milrem fire baseless.
verdict_note: Two national services point the same way, detentions and seizures are confirmed, and the method matches earlier proven GRU proxy cases.

claim: Russia has put in writing a demand that NATO pull forces and bases back to 1997 positions, which would remove them from Poland, the Baltic states and Finland
claimed_by: The New York Times and The Telegraph (leaked 10 November paper)
conflict: Peskov said on 13 November that no withdrawal of NATO members was discussed; the paper is unsigned and unpublished.
verdict_note: No new information since yesterday; Peskov's denial concerns members leaving NATO, not a pull-back of forces, so it does not rule out the paper.

claim: Russia asked that Finland leave NATO
claimed_by: Bild (anonymous sources)
conflict: The Kremlin denies it; Finland's defence minister rejects any such terms; accounts of the leaked paper do not mention it.
verdict_note: Still rests on one anonymous-source report against an on-the-record denial.

claim: Estonia's border closure is an act of Russophobia
claimed_by: Russian foreign ministry spokeswoman Maria Zakharova
conflict: Estonia ties the closure to a specific sabotage attempt that two security services attribute to Russia.
verdict_note: The closure is a stated response to an attack, not aimed at Russians as such; it will however hurt cross-border residents.

claim: Europe does not want peace, so talks on European security may be pointless
claimed_by: Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov
conflict: European states have formed a negotiating team and say they want to join talks; the Kremlin itself says Europe has not yet contacted it.
verdict_note: A framing that shifts blame for stalled talks onto Europe; no evidence offered.

claim: The pro-UPA graffiti on Polish monuments is the work of Ukrainian nationalists
claimed_by: Polish social media; anti-Ukrainian commentators
conflict: A Ukrainian teenager was detained, but a local portal reports a Telegram channel paying 500 dollars per job, and Ukraine's embassy blames Russian hybrid tactics; Polish authorities have not attributed it.
verdict_note: Who did it is established in one case only; who paid for it is unknown.

claim: Russia's GRU ordered the attempted arson at Threod Systems in Estonia
claimed_by: Estonia's KAPO, prosecutor general and foreign minister; supported by Latvia's VDD
conflict: The Kremlin now explicitly calls the accusation entirely baseless; neither side has published its evidence.
verdict_note: Detentions, court custody requests and seizures in two countries back the Estonian account; the denial offers no alternative explanation.

claim: Estonia's accusations of Russian sabotage are entirely baseless
claimed_by: Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov
conflict: Estonia and Latvia point to physical evidence and detentions; Russia has denied earlier attributions later supported in European courts.
verdict_note: A blanket denial with no evidence or counter-explanation.

claim: Estonia's border closure is Russophobia, and a wall that will harm those who build it
claimed_by: Russian foreign ministry spokeswoman Maria Zakharova; Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov
conflict: Estonia ties the closure to a specific sabotage attempt and to sanctions evasion, not to Russians as such.
verdict_note: The closure is a stated security response; it will hurt cross-border residents, which the framing exploits.

claim: Russia has put in writing a demand that NATO pull forces and bases back to 1997 positions, which would remove them from Poland, the Baltic states and Finland
claimed_by: The New York Times, The Economist and The Telegraph (leaked paper); repeated by Al Jazeera
conflict: Peskov said on 13 November that no withdrawal of NATO members was discussed; the paper is unsigned and unpublished.
verdict_note: Several outlets describe the same document, and Russia's chief negotiator publicly calls a new European security system the central topic; Peskov's denial does not cover a pull-back of forces.

claim: Estonia has destroyed at least 140 Soviet war memorials in an act of historical vandalism
claimed_by: Russia's chargé d'affaires in Tallinn, via RIA Novosti; repeated by Izvestia, RT and others
conflict: Propastop notes Estonia catalogued 322 monuments and marked 244 for removal or replacement, while war graves are maintained; the figure of 140 is not explained.
verdict_note: Removing Soviet monuments is a real policy, but the claim merges it with war graves and remembrance to suggest an attack on the dead.

claim: The Polish sabotage threat was invented to justify tighter controls
claimed_by: Anti-government and Russia-friendly social media accounts in Poland (per a Warsaw security firm's monitoring)
conflict: Polish prosecutors have confirmed the November 2025 rail sabotage and other acts, with detentions and charges.
verdict_note: Sabotage in Poland is documented by investigations and court cases; the narrative minimises them.

claim: The pro-UPA graffiti on Polish monuments is the work of Ukrainian nationalists
claimed_by: Polish social media; anti-Ukrainian commentators
conflict: One Ukrainian teenager has been charged in the Tri-City; others are unknown, and no one has been detained in Warsaw. Ukraine's embassy blames Russia, which Polish authorities have not confirmed.
verdict_note: Who did it is established in one case only; who paid for it is unknown.

claim: Russia's GRU ordered the attempted arson at Threod Systems in Estonia
claimed_by: Estonia's security police, prosecutor general and foreign minister; supported by Latvia's VDD
conflict: The Kremlin calls the accusation baseless; neither side has published its evidence. New: Estonia's security police says it had advance intelligence of the attack.
verdict_note: Detentions, court custody and seizures in two countries back the Estonian account; the denial offers no alternative explanation.

claim: Closing Estonia's border with Russia would not have prevented the Milrem and Threod attacks
claimed_by: Estonian President Ülle Madise
conflict: The foreign minister tied the closure directly to the Threod attack, saying Russia's hostile acts come at a cost; the prime minister wants the closure to be indefinite.
verdict_note: The Threod suspects were residents of Latvia recruited remotely, so a road closure would not have stopped them; the closure targets other risks, such as travel used for recruitment.

claim: Russia has put in writing a demand that NATO pull forces and bases back to 1997 positions, which would remove them from Poland, the Baltic states and Finland
claimed_by: The New York Times, The Economist and The Telegraph (leaked paper)
conflict: Peskov said on 13 November that no withdrawal of NATO members was discussed; on 17 November Lavrov said Moscow remains committed to its 2021 demands, which included such a pull-back.
verdict_note: Lavrov's on-record statement supports the substance; the document itself is still unpublished.

claim: Europe is trying to squeeze into peace talks to build a security system aimed against Russia
claimed_by: Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov
conflict: EU governments say they seek a role because Europe's own security is at stake; NATO's secretary general says Russia is the one trying to weaken Europe.
verdict_note: European states are directly affected by any settlement; presenting their participation as a plot against Russia reverses who is demanding changes to European security.

claim: The Polish sabotage threat was invented or exaggerated to justify tighter controls
claimed_by: Anti-government and Russia-friendly social media accounts in Poland (per a Warsaw security firm's monitoring)
conflict: New: the monitor's 17 November report lists four confirmed acts of sabotage, 15 detentions and two attacks classed as terrorism, with trials pending, and notes an 'only four acts' line used to play the threat down.
verdict_note: Sabotage in Poland is documented by investigations and charges; the narrative minimises it.

claim: Russian intelligence planned a mass-casualty false-flag attack near the Polish–Kaliningrad border in late October or early November, to be blamed on Ukraine
claimed_by: Rzeczpospolita, citing anonymous senior sources close to Poland's military and security services; repeated by The Telegraph, European Pravda, Kyiv Post and Meduza
conflict: All accounts trace back to one newspaper's sources. Versions differ: Rzeczpospolita describes an operation on Polish territory, while The Telegraph's retelling says Russian civilians in the Kaliningrad area would have been the victims. Poland's special-services coordinator Tomasz Siemoniak would neither confirm nor deny details and said only that the threat was judged real. No Russian response found; Moscow has itself accused Ukraine of plotting false flags in Poland before.
verdict_note: Plausible given the early-November border alert and reinforcements, but resting on anonymous sources with no official confirmation; one outlet repeated by many counts as one source.

claim: Russia has offered to reduce its military presence in Kaliningrad and Belarus if NATO pulls back to its 1997 footprint
claimed_by: Bloomberg and the New York Times, citing sources and a document setting out Moscow's negotiating position; Kyiv Post headline says Russia would pull troops from Kaliningrad
conflict: Two major outlets describe the same document, but no official has confirmed it. Meduza notes it is unclear what a reduction would involve; the Kyiv Post headline about pulling troops out goes further than the reporting. European governments reportedly say Russia must stop fighting in Ukraine before any NATO discussion.
verdict_note: Consistent with Moscow's public 2021 demands and Lavrov's restatement this week; the size and meaning of the offered reduction are unknown.

claim: Russia is setting up extra ammunition and fuel depots and field communication hubs in Kaliningrad, Belarus and its Moscow and Leningrad military districts
claimed_by: Yevhen Yerin, spokesperson for Ukraine's military intelligence (HUR), presenting a report in Kyiv on 18 November
conflict: No locations, numbers or imagery were published, and no other government or open-source analyst has confirmed it today. It fits the Lithuanian baseline's description of long-term Russian rebuilding near NATO, and HUR itself judges a direct attack unlikely for now.
verdict_note: An on-the-record claim from an intelligence service that is a party to the war, without published evidence; plausible but not verified.

claim: A direct Russian military attack on the Baltic states or Poland is unlikely while the war in Ukraine continues
claimed_by: Ukraine's military intelligence (18 November); Lithuania's 2026 National Threat Assessment
conflict: No source in today's reporting contradicts the near-term judgement. The Lithuanian assessment adds that Russia could carry out limited operations against NATO states in the longer term, and HUR warns of provocations against military and logistics sites.
verdict_note: Two independent intelligence judgements agree, and no indicator shows forces being moved toward the Baltic states.

claim: Estonia's border closure is driven by Russophobia rather than a real security threat
claimed_by: Russian Foreign Ministry spokeswoman Maria Zakharova; Russian state media
conflict: Estonia links the closure to GRU-attributed sabotage against its defence firms, backed by arrests and court-ordered custody. Estonian critics, including Narva's mayor and the president, question the cost and whether it fits the threat, but not the security reasons behind it.
verdict_note: The closure is a security measure that applies to all travellers and follows documented sabotage; its humanitarian costs for families are real, but the Russophobia framing leaves out the stated reasons.

claim: Russian intelligence planned a mass-casualty false-flag attack near the Polish–Kaliningrad border in late October or early November, to be blamed on Ukraine
claimed_by: Rzeczpospolita, citing anonymous senior sources; repeated by many outlets
conflict: Still one newspaper's sources. Poland's police chief said on record on 2 November that the border operation followed warnings of possible sabotage there, and the special-services coordinator said only that the threat was judged real. No government has confirmed the false-flag element, and retellings differ on who the victims would have been.
verdict_note: Plausible given the confirmed alert, but the specific plan rests on anonymous sources; no new evidence today.

claim: Russia has offered to reduce its military presence in Kaliningrad and Belarus if NATO pulls back to its 1997 footprint
claimed_by: Bloomberg and the New York Times, citing Russia's negotiating paper; repeated by Meduza and others
conflict: Consistent with Russia's public demands for a NATO rollback, and with an earlier BILD report of informal proposals including removing NATO bases from the Baltic states. The Kremlin has not confirmed the Kaliningrad element and earlier denied demanding that Finland leave NATO.
verdict_note: Two major outlets report the same document; what a reduction would mean is unclear.

claim: Russia is setting up extra ammunition and fuel depots and field communication hubs near NATO borders and in Belarus
claimed_by: Ukraine's military intelligence, repeated by a spokesman on 18 November
conflict: No imagery, locations or numbers published; ISW reported nothing significant on Belarus the same day. Western and Baltic officials have not echoed the claim.
verdict_note: A plausible claim from an interested party, not yet supported by independent evidence.

claim: Russia's information campaign is preparing a pretext for possible aggression against NATO's eastern flank
claimed_by: Ukraine's foreign ministry spokesman, citing a Centre for Countering Disinformation study (18 November)
conflict: Information operations against the Baltic states are well documented, including by the Lithuanian baseline. But Ukraine's military intelligence called a direct attack unlikely while the war continues, Baltic officials say border threat levels have not risen, and the ministry itself said no one knows whether an attack will happen.
verdict_note: The information-pressure part is supported; the link to attack preparation is a judgement without military evidence.

claim: NATO is assessing more troops and the deployment of nuclear weapons in Lithuania and Poland
claimed_by: Head of Russia's delegation at the OSCE Forum for Security Co-operation, via TASS
conflict: Lithuania is debating removing its constitutional ban on hosting nuclear weapons (final vote expected in January) and has offered to fund a permanent US base, but no NATO decision or plan to station nuclear weapons in either country has been reported.
verdict_note: Mixes a real domestic debate with an unsupported claim about NATO deployment plans.

claim: Estonia's border closure is driven by Russophobia rather than a real security threat
claimed_by: Russian Foreign Ministry spokeswoman Maria Zakharova
conflict: Estonia's security service says the 14 November arson attempt at a drone maker was ordered by Russian military intelligence and carried out by residents of Latvia, eight of whom were detained; Estonia's government says the closure answers repeated hybrid attacks.
verdict_note: Ignores the stated security reasons; whether closure is the right response is debated in Estonia, but the threat is documented.

claim: Russia deliberately timed missiles to land in Poland near a Coalition of the Willing exercise
claimed_by: Polish Defence Minister Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz and Prime Minister Donald Tusk
conflict: The impact sites were roughly 35–75 km from the exercise and 30–60 km from the Ukrainian border, during a strike of up to 100 missiles on Ukraine. Poland has published no evidence on flight paths. Trump described earlier incursions as mistakes; Moscow has not commented.
verdict_note: That Russian missiles landed in Poland is confirmed; intent and deliberate timing are judgements not yet supported by published evidence.

claim: Putin has sent drones and missiles into Poland only by mistake
claimed_by: US President Donald Trump, in a Fox News interview on 19 November
conflict: Polish officials call recent incursions deliberate provocations; the 2025 drone incursion led to Article 4 consultations. No investigation has published findings on intent for the latest case.
verdict_note: Trump gave no evidence; whether past incursions were accidental is disputed, and his remark predates the 20 November landings.

claim: Russian intelligence planned a mass-casualty false-flag attack near the Polish–Kaliningrad border, to be blamed on Ukraine
claimed_by: Rzeczpospolita, citing anonymous senior sources; repeated by many outlets
conflict: Polish officials confirmed an alert and a real sabotage threat in early November, but no government has confirmed the false-flag element.
verdict_note: No new evidence today.

claim: Estonia's border closure is Russophobia and a new Iron Curtain rather than a response to a real threat
claimed_by: Russian Foreign Ministry spokeswoman Maria Zakharova; Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov called the sabotage accusations unfounded
conflict: Estonia's security service says the 14 November arson attempt was ordered by Russian military intelligence and eight people were detained. Whether closing the border is proportionate is debated inside Estonia, including by its president.
verdict_note: Ignores the documented security case; the policy choice itself is legitimately debated.

claim: Russia has offered to reduce its military presence in Kaliningrad and Belarus if NATO pulls back to its 1997 footprint
claimed_by: Bloomberg and the New York Times, citing Russia's negotiating paper
conflict: Consistent with Russia's public demands; the Kremlin has not confirmed the Kaliningrad element, and the 19 November trilateral meeting produced no agreement on Ukraine or European security.
verdict_note: No new information today; two major outlets report the same document.

claim: Russia deliberately timed missiles to land in Poland near a Coalition of the Willing exercise
claimed_by: Polish Defence Minister Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz and Prime Minister Donald Tusk; ISW assessed that Russia timed the incursions to test NATO
conflict: The impact sites were roughly 30–60 km from the Ukrainian border during a massive strike on Ukraine. Poland has published no flight-path evidence. The Kremlin denies any violation.
verdict_note: That Russian missiles landed in Poland is confirmed; deliberate timing is a judgement shared by Poland and ISW but not yet shown by published evidence.

claim: Poland admits it has no proof the missiles were Russian
claimed_by: Sputnik (Russian state media), citing Foreign Minister Radosław Sikorski
conflict: Sikorski said Poland is awaiting confirmation of concrete facts; the defence minister has identified one object as a Kh-101, and NATO calls it a Russian violation.
verdict_note: Turns caution during an investigation into a supposed admission.

claim: Claims that Russia violated Polish airspace are empty and groundless
claimed_by: Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov
conflict: Polish officials identified missile wreckage at three sites, and NATO's secretary general called it a grave violation. Russia gave no alternative explanation.
verdict_note: Strongly contradicted by the physical evidence and by Poland and NATO; the investigation continues.

claim: A Swedish Gripen had NATO clearance to shoot down the Kh-101 but held fire due to bad weather
claimed_by: Rzeczpospolita, as reported by the Kyiv Post
conflict: No confirmation from Sweden, Poland or NATO in the sources found.
verdict_note: Single-outlet report.

claim: Ukraine carried out the drone strike on the Russian ship Sparta II
claimed_by: Finland's Defence Forces ('quite possibly'); Finnish Prime Minister Petteri Orpo defended Ukraine's right to fight back
conflict: No one has claimed the strike; Russian officials did not name an attacker; Ukraine's foreign ministry did not respond. The vessel serves Russia's defence ministry, a type of target Ukraine has hit before.
verdict_note: Plausible and widely assumed, but not attributed by evidence or claim.

claim: A suspicious aerial object approached Kaliningrad from Lithuania
claimed_by: Kaliningrad governor Alexey Besprozvannykh
conflict: The governor himself said specialists found no threat; no evidence or Lithuanian comment was found.
verdict_note: No evidence published; fits a recurring Russian narrative about the Baltic states.

claim: All three objects that entered Polish airspace on 20 November were Russian Kh-101 cruise missiles
claimed_by: Lublin District Prosecutor's Office (preliminary findings, 22 November)
conflict: Poland's defence ministry first spoke of two missiles and a probable jet-powered drone; one specialist outlet still reports doubt about two of the objects. The Kremlin denies any violation.
verdict_note: Based on debris at three sites; the final site check was due on 23 November.

claim: NATO, Poland, Lithuania or German troops in Poland were behind the Kaliningrad alert
claimed_by: Russian media and Telegram channels, after the governor's remark about an object from the direction of Lithuania
conflict: Poland's counter-disinformation centre called the claims false; Lithuania's foreign minister rejected them and its air force detected no drones. No evidence has been published.
verdict_note: No evidence supports any NATO or Baltic role.

claim: Drones struck the Baltic Fleet base at Baltiysk on 21 November
claimed_by: Ukrainian Telegram channels; some Ukrainian and international headlines
conflict: Air-defence fire was geolocated to the port area, but no damage is verified, Ukraine has not claimed it and Russia denies any threat. A widely shared fire photo was from Iran.
verdict_note: Something triggered air defences; a hit is not shown.

claim: A Russian helicopter violated Finnish airspace off Loviisa on 21 November
claimed_by: Finland's Ministry of Defence (suspected violation)
conflict: Defence Minister Antti Häkkänen said it was possibly linked to the rescue or monitoring of the Sparta II. Russia has not commented.
verdict_note: Investigation by the Finnish Border Guard is still open.

claim: Ukraine carried out the drone strike on the Russian ship Sparta II
claimed_by: Finland's Defence Forces ('likely'); Estonia's foreign minister called the strike a consequence of Russia's war
conflict: Ukraine has not commented. Accounts of the location differ: Finland's Border Guard chief said Russian territorial waters; Finnish defence officials and a Russian governor said international waters near the border.
